tagline: Along the state line, after a narrow gauge long gone.
intro: Out of Durango the byway crosses Southern Ute reservation land to Ignacio, then goes on past Arboles and the north end of Navajo Lake toward Chama, New Mexico, 125 miles in all along the Colorado and New Mexico line.

Its story is the Denver and Rio Grande, which laid three-foot narrow gauge because it was cheaper and took tighter curves, and reached Chama on the last day of 1880 on its way to Durango. The rails from Chama west to Durango were abandoned in 1967 and torn up soon after. East of Chama the line still runs, under steam, as the Cumbres and Toltec.

moments.title: Ignacio
moments.text: The Southern Ute Indian Tribe keeps its headquarters and its cultural center and museum in this town of about 850, called Piinuu in Ute.

moments.title: Arboles
moments.text: Arboles, Spanish for trees, takes in 650 acres of water, and the lake behind the 1962 Navajo Dam moved almost 200 families out of four communities, Los Arboles among them.

moments.title: Chimney Rock National Monument
moments.text: A round-trip spur off the byway leads to a Chacoan great house of 36 rooms on a sandstone ridge, begun in 1076 when the moon stood between Chimney Rock and Companion Rock.

practical: Mobile phone service is limited or missing over parts of the route.
